Uganda's Ministry of Health declared the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak ended on 28 July 2026: 20 confirmed cases, 18 recoveries, 2 deaths, all confined to Kampala and Wakiso, 15 imported from DRC and 5 secondary. Declaration rests on a 'fully documented importation event' — source identified, all transmission chains reconstructed, all 836 contacts closed — counting 42 days from the 16 June discharge of the last Ugandan national, rather than the 16 July date WHO AFRO used when it announced the countdown. NO ENTRY REQUIREMENT HAS CHANGED AS A RESULT: US restrictions run to at least 12 August and DRC transmission continues. Quote the declaration, not a lifting of rules.
items.source: Uganda Ministry of Health / Uganda Media Centre, 28 Jul 2026

items.who: Travellers arriving in the US who were in Uganda or South Sudan in the past 21 days
items.effective: Renewed 12 August 2026, 5:00pm EDT — in force to 4:59pm EDT Friday 11 September 2026
items.note: CDC renewed the order on 12 Aug 2026 (signed PDF August-T42-Order_08.11.2026-signed.pdf). Uganda was NOT decoupled despite the 28 Jul Ebola-free declaration. US citizens and nationals from Uganda/South Sudan are not restricted but are rerouted to Dulles (IAD), Atlanta (ATL), Houston (IAH) or JFK for public health entry screening; US lawful permanent residents are named as restricted. Anyone in the DRC within 21 days — US citizens included — cannot board a US-bound flight. Note CDC's own legal-authorities page still listed the 13 Jul order as current when checked on 13 Aug. UPDATE 16 AUG: full text now readable — FR Doc 2026-16706, filed 14 Aug 08:45, publication date 17 Aug 2026, docket CDC-2026-0892. Continues the July order WITHOUT CHANGE and expires 4:59pm EDT Fri 11 Sep 2026. The operative determination reads Ebola is “confirmed currently present in DRC and RECENTLY present in Uganda” — past tense for Uganda — yet Uganda stays on the covered list on the stated ground of “continued overland travel from DRC”. The release condition is therefore DRC-side: the order cites contact tracing at ~78% against a 95% operational threshold| true outbreak size possibly two to four times greater than reported| and DRC at 4|318 confirmed / 2|011 deaths across 53 health zones as at 9 Aug (vs 1|873 / 672 across 41 zones at the 13 Jul order). CDC response is at Level 1| the highest in its Graduated Response Framework. A 15-DAY COMMENT PERIOD opens on publication 17 Aug and closes on or about 1 Sep| before the 11 Sep assessment: comments received to date were 3 (original+amended)| 5 (June)| and NONE on the July renewal. Uganda THN remains Level 2; Level 4 covers Ituri and North Kivu only.

items.note: Materially harsher than the US rule and widely missed. Under the Quarantine Act, travellers from Uganda or South Sudan may enter Canada but must quarantine 21 days on arrival unless exempt. Anyone in the DRC within 21 days is prohibited from entering Canada or boarding a Canada-bound flight. Brief Canadian guests SEPARATELY from US guests — a single 'North America' line in pre-arrival comms is wrong for both.
items.source: travel.gc.ca health notice 550, modified 23 Jul 2026 / Public Health Agency of Canada

items.rule: US Ebola entry restrictions & airport screening
items.amount: No fee — screening and entry limits
items.who: Anyone who has been in DRC, Uganda or South Sudan in the previous 21 days, regardless of nationality — INCLUDING US lawful permanent residents
items.effective: Order signed 13 July 2026, in force to 4:59pm EDT Wednesday 12 August 2026
items.note: CDC order under PHS Act ss.362/365, published at 91 FR 43636 on 16 July 2026, docket CDC-2026-0892. THE GREEN CARD EXEMPTION IS GONE: 42 CFR 71.40(f) was amended on 27 May 2026 (91 FR 31362) and the order applies expressly to lawful permanent residents. Exempt: US citizens and nationals, US military and government personnel on orders, and case-by-case CBP/CDC exceptions. DHS separately funnels affected flights to Washington Dulles (IAD) under 91 FR 29896, 21 May 2026. The order names Nairobi JKIA, Addis Ababa, Doha, Dubai, Brussels and Istanbul as transit corridors of concern — Kenya itself is NOT restricted. PUBLIC COMMENT CLOSES 31 JULY 2026 at regulations.gov under docket CDC-2026-0892; CDC has already refused, in writing, a request to assess Uganda independently of DRC. Next decision point 12 August. UPDATE 29 JUL: Uganda's Ministry of Health declared the outbreak OVER on 28 July 2026 — thirty days before the diarised ~27 August all-clear — so the 12 August renewal now falls AFTER a formal end-of-outbreak declaration, not before it. As at 08:00 EAT 29 July we can find no WHO statement endorsing the declaration and no change to the CDC order or the US Level 4 advisory. Sell 'outbreak over', not 'restrictions lifted'. UPDATE 5 AUG: WHO DON614 (1 Aug| revised 3 Aug) reports epidemiological week 30 as the outbreak's worst week yet (567 cases| 296 deaths) and confirms it is now the largest Ebola outbreak on record in DRC (3|605 confirmed| 1|587 deaths| 44% CFR). A WHO IHR Emergency Committee meets 18 August — six days after the 12 Aug US renewal point. UPDATE 20 AUG: the committee met on 18 Aug (its second meeting). WHO AFRO 18 Aug report: 5|021 confirmed / 2|378 deaths across 55 health zones in six provinces (Ituri 4|257/1|878; North Kivu 607/428 across 12 of 34 zones; South Kivu first 3 cases/1 death) — up from 4|318/2|011 on 9 Aug, and now creeping into provinces bordering Uganda and Rwanda. Advisory levels and entry orders unchanged; next US assessment 11 Sep.
90-day multiple entry, free movement between the three. Apply through your FIRST country of entry. Materially cheaper than three separate visas — sell multi-country itineraries on it.
